topic: would rather / had better / it's time

questions.q: I'd rather you ___ smoking in the house.
questions.explanation: 'Would rather' about someone else takes the past simple.

questions.q: You'd better ___ your passport before we leave.
questions.explanation: 'Had better' is followed by the bare infinitive.

questions.q: It's time you ___ a decision.
questions.explanation: 'It's time' with a subject takes the past simple for present meaning.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I'd rather to stay at home than go out tonight.
I'd rather stay at home than go out tonight.
I'd rather staying at home than go out tonight.
I'd rather stayed at home than go out tonight.
questions.explanation: 'Would rather' takes the bare infinitive, not 'to' or '-ing'.

questions.q: She'd rather her son ___ medicine than law.
questions.explanation: 'Would rather' with a different subject takes the past simple.

questions.q: We'd better hurry, ___ we?
questions.explanation: The question tag after ''d better' uses 'hadn't'.

questions.q: It's high time they ___ the problem seriously.
questions.explanation: 'It's high time' takes the past simple for something overdue.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: You'd better to not be late again.
You had better not to be late again.
You'd better not be late again.
You'd better don't be late again.
questions.explanation: 'Had better' takes the bare infinitive, with 'not' before it.

questions.q: I'd rather ___ by train than fly.
questions.explanation: 'Would rather' is followed by the bare infinitive.

questions.q: It's about time he ___ his own flat.
questions.explanation: 'It's about time' takes the past simple.

questions.q: You had better ___ to the doctor about that cough.
questions.explanation: 'Had better' is followed by the bare infinitive.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I'd rather you came with us tomorrow.
I'd rather you come with us tomorrow.
I'd rather you will come with us tomorrow.
I'd rather you would come with us tomorrow.
questions.explanation: 'Would rather' about another person takes the past simple, even for the future.

questions.q: I'd rather have ___ at home last night.
questions.explanation: 'Would rather have' for a past preference takes the past participle.

questions.q: It's time for bed — you'd better ___ up now.
questions.explanation: 'Had better' takes the bare infinitive.

questions.q: She'd rather not ___ about it.
questions.explanation: Put 'not' before the bare infinitive after 'would rather'.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: It's time we leave — the film starts in ten minutes.
It's time we will leave — the film starts in ten minutes.
It's time us to leave — the film starts in ten minutes.
It's time we left — the film starts in ten minutes.
questions.explanation: 'It's time' with a subject takes the past simple.

questions.q: We'd rather you ___ the news to her gently.
questions.explanation: 'Would rather' with another subject takes the past simple.

questions.q: You'd better ___ your seatbelt.
questions.explanation: 'Had better' is followed by the bare infinitive.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I'd rather to have a coffee than a tea.
I'd rather having a coffee than a tea.
I'd prefer rather have a coffee than a tea.
I'd rather have a coffee than a tea.
questions.explanation: 'Would rather' takes the bare infinitive after it.

questions.q: It's high time the government ___ action.
questions.explanation: 'It's high time' takes the past simple for an overdue action.
